changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: Stop pricing changes from being a tax on the roadmap. Change a price, launch a trial or set up proration in a few clicks, and give your engineers back the quarter a pricing change takes today. For product and engineering buyers on a homegrown billing system. Keep revenue growth as a secondary point for finance.
changes.why: The champion explicitly rejected the revenue framing and called billing 'a tax on the roadmap', and the demo landed when it showed a quarter of roadmap saved in five minutes.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: Your own number, not an average. In a working session we build what your current billing costs you: engineering time on pricing changes, billing errors and lapsed subscriptions. You walk into finance with 'a number that's ours'. For champions who must get a purchase past a CFO.
changes.why: The champion said he could not get the deal past the CFO without a number that was Pikeview's own, and the generic ROI deck with the study was all we sent after he asked for payback.

changes.change: Add a migration reference story from a customer who moved a homegrown billing system over in stages without asking customers for their card details again, with an offer to put the buyer on a call with that customer. Use it alongside the staged-migration doc for buyers with existing subscriptions.
changes.why: Owen asked about moving existing subscriptions without re-collecting card details and about doing it in stages, and wanted to talk to someone who had done it, but we had no reference to offer.

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: Use this line for subscription businesses that lose customers to failed cards: 'Subscriptions lapse because a card fails and nobody chases it. Recover them automatically, and count what that is worth in your own numbers.' Pair it with the cost-of-status-quo session.
changes.why: Owen himself named lapsed landlord subscriptions from failed cards as a cost we could have quantified, which matches our recovery capability but was never added up.
